extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, proofs, and exercises about semicontinuity of cohomology, Grauert's theorem, the Cohomology and Base Change theorem, Mumford's key theorem (complex of free modules), and applications to moduli (Grassmannian, hypersurfaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity Theorem (28.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes, and F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y. Then for each p the function Y → Z given by q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is an upper semicontinuous function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation: ranks of cohomology groups are upper semicontinuous in proper flat families. A proof is given in §28.2.4. Use complexes of free modules (Mumford's idea) to reduce to linear-algebra statements (ranks/minors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning / example: cohomology can jump (28.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology groups of fibers may jump in flat families: example of an elliptic curve (E,p0) and a line bundle L whose h^0(E,L|_p) is generically 0 but jumps to 1 at p = p0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows that cohomology does not always commute with base change; semicontinuity only guarantees upper semicontinuity, not constancy. Use such examples to check hypotheses (e.g., smoothness, characteristic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grauert's Theorem (28.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is proper, Y is reduced and locally Noetherian, F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y, and h^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is a locally constant function of q ∈ Y, then R^p π_* F is locally free and the base-change map φ^p_Z is an isomorphism for all ψ : Z → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other words: locally constant fiber dimensions (over a reduced base) allow the cohomology groups to fit together into a vector bundle and identify fibers of the pushforward with the cohomology of fibers. No Noetherian hypotheses are needed for some versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology and Base Change Theorem (28.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π is proper, Y is locally Noetherian, F is coherent on X and flat over Y, and φ^p_q is surjective at a point q. Then (i) there is an open neighborhood U of q such that for any ψ : Z → U the base-change map φ^p_Z is an isomorphism; (ii) furthermore φ^{p-1}_q is an isomorphism. Equivalently, φ^p_q surjective iff R^p π_* F is locally free in some neighborhood of q (equivalently (R^p π_* F)_q is a free O_{Y,q}-module), which implies h^p is constant in a neighborhood of q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hypothesis that φ^p_q is surjective involves only reduced points but gives implications on the (possibly nonreduced) scheme as a whole. The local criterion for flatness is a key technical ingredient in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dense-open local freeness consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is integral, π is proper, and F is coherent on X flat over Y, then by semicontinuity there is a dense open subset of Y on which R^p π_* F is locally free and the fiber of the pth higher pushforward is the pth cohomology of the fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Semicontinuity Theorem 28.1.1 to locate the dense open where ranks are constant; then apply Grauert/Cohomology and Base Change to deduce local freeness and identification of fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for a line bundle to descend (Proposition 28.1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is flat, proper, O-connected morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, Y reduced, and L is an invertible sheaf on X that is trivial on the fibers of π. Then π_* L is an invertible sheaf M on Y and the natural map π^* π_* L → L is an isomorphism (i.e., L is the pullback of M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Grauert's Theorem to identify π_*L on fibers with H^0(X_q, L_q) and Nakayama's lemma to deduce surjectivity on fibers implies global isomorphism. This gives a method to recover line bundles on the base from fiberwise trivial line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mumford's Key Theorem (28.2.1): free complex representing cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Spec B is proper and F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Spec B. Then there is a complex · · · → K^{-1} → K^0 → K^1 → ··· → K^n → 0 of finitely generated free B-modules and an isomorphism of functors H^p(K^• ⊗_B A) ≅ H^p(X ×_B Spec A, F ⊗_B A) for all p and for all ring maps B → A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This turns questions about pushforwards and base change into linear algebra about complexes of free modules (matrices over B). Semicontinuity becomes the statement that ranks of matrices drop on closed subsets; base change questions become statements about flatness/freeness of cokernels, kernels, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of finite free complex quasi-isomorphic to a given complex (Lemma 28.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let B be Noetherian. If C^• is a complex with cohomology H^i(C^•) finitely generated and C^p = 0 for p > n, then there exists a complex K^• of finite rank free B-modules with K^p = 0 for p > n and a morphism α: K^• → C^• inducing isomorphisms H^i(K^•) ≅ H^i(C^•) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma is the technical device to replace Čech complexes or other complexes with an explicit finite free model suitable for base change arguments; it is built inductively and is used in the proof of Mumford's theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-isomorphism commutes with arbitrary base change for flat bounded complexes (Lemma 28.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α: K^• → C^• is a morphism of complexes of flat B-modules bounded on the right inducing isomorphisms on cohomology (a quasi-isomorphism), then for every B-algebra A the induced map α ⊗_B A: K^• ⊗_B A → C^• ⊗_B A induces isomorphisms on cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the mapping cone; exactness of the mapping cone is preserved after tensoring with A because the mapping cone is exact and all modules are flat. This justifies checking cohomology after arbitrary base change using the finite free model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear-algebra technique for Semicontinuity (28.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a finite free complex K^• as in Mumford's theorem, dim_{κ(q)} H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) = dim_{κ(q)} ker(δ_p ⊗ κ(q)) − dim_{κ(q)} im(δ_{p-1} ⊗ κ(q)) − dim_{κ(q)} im(δ_p ⊗ κ(q)). The dimensions of the images are lower semicontinuous because loci where their rank drops are defined by minors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus semicontinuity reduces to the elementary fact that rank conditions on matrices are closed conditions (minors vanish). See (28.2.4.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: New proof of constancy of Euler characteristic in flat families (28.2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the finite free complex K^• and a modification J^• with J^p = K^p for p ≥ 0 and J^{−1} = ker(K^0 → K^1), one gets χ(X_q, F|_{X_q}) = Σ (−1)^p rank J^p, hence the Euler characteristic is locally constant in flat proper families (Theorem 24.7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: construct J^• with same cohomology for p ≥ 0, show J^{−1} is coherent and flat (hence locally free), and then compute alternating sum of ranks. The mapping cone exactness and flatness arguments are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness / local freeness criteria from complexes (28.2.E–28.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If W_p K^• and W_{p+1} K^• (cokernels of differentials) are flat at a point, then base change maps φ^p and φ^{p-1} are isomorphisms in a neighborhood and H^p(K^•) is locally free there. Conversely, surjectivity of φ^p_q implies flatness of certain cokernels and thus local freeness of H^p in a neighborhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proofs proceed by analyzing the exact sequences relating Z_p, B_p, W_p, H_p and applying right-exact functors and the local criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.6.2). The boxed 'snake' diagrams in §28.2.6 are the technical heart of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing Noetherian hypotheses via finite presentation (28.2.9–28.2.M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noetherian hypotheses in the theorems of §28.1 can be removed if one imposes finite-presentation hypotheses: if π : X → Spec B is finitely presented and F finitely presented quasi-coherent, one can descend to a Noetherian base Spec Z[x_1,…,x_N]/I and deduce versions of constancy of Euler characteristic, semicontinuity, Grauert, and Cohomology and Base Change under finite-presentation assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 28.2.L constructs such a base-change diagram. However, finite-presentation hypotheses are necessary: there are counterexamples when finite-presentation fails (28.2.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: representability of families (Grassmannian, hypersurfaces) using cohomology & base change (§28.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: To show a functor of flat finitely presented families is representable (e.g., Grassmannian G(k,n) or degree-d hypersurfaces Hd,n), use cohomology & base change to prove vanishing of higher cohomology on fibers, show R^i π_* O_X(1) are locally free of prescribed ranks, obtain short exact sequences of locally free sheaves (e.g., 0 → I_X(1) → π_* O_{P^{n-1}_B}(1) → π_* O_X(1) → 0), and hence produce the canonical quotient maps (O^n_B → π_* O_X(1)) that give the universal object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely: for a family X ⊂ P^{n-1}_B with fibers P^{k-1}, O_X(1) restricts to O(1) on fibers (so higher cohomology vanishes), R^i π_* O_X(1) is locally free of rank k, and the surjection O^n_B → π_* O_X(1) produces the representing map to the Grassmannian. For hypersurfaces, construct the universal hypersurface X ⊂ P^n × P^N and verify flatness and finite presentation.
